bib.title: OdysseyBench: Evaluating LLM Agents on Long-Horizon Complex Office Application Workflows

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "OdysseyBench: Evaluating LLM Agents on Long-Horizon Complex Office Application Workflows", Weixuan Wang, Dongge Han, Daniel Madrigal Diaz, Jin Xu, Victor Rühle, Saravan Rajmohan. Preprint; the only venue printed is "arXiv:2508.09124v1 [cs.CL] 12 Aug 2025". First author: School of Informatics, University of Edinburgh (work done during an internship at Microsoft); all other authors Microsoft.

COVERAGE: 21 of 21 pages, 71,232 of 71,232 chars. References (pp. 13-15) were skimmed for origins; appendices A-B (verifier criteria, generation prompts, pp. 16-21) were read.

CLAIMS

1. How the tasks were made
- Two splits: 300 tasks adapted from OfficeBench and 302 generated from scratch. Quote (p.1): "OdysseyBench+ with 300 tasks derived from real-world use cases, and OdysseyBench-Neo with 302 newly synthesized complex tasks".
- In the + split, the task and its checker come from OfficeBench. A GPT-4.1 generator/verifier loop (max 5 iterations) writes only the task intent and a multi-day dialogue around it.
- In the Neo split, an orchestrator, per-app "surfers", a task generator and a dialogue generator (all GPT-4.1, built on Magentic-One) produce the task, the evaluation criteria and the dialogues.
- The dialogue assistant never executes anything; it replies "will do". The history is therefore instructions plus chitchat, not real prior work.
- Size (Table 1, p.7): 602 tasks, split 153 / 166 / 283 for one / two / three apps. Histories average 3,468.9 tokens (+) and 5,169.9 tokens (Neo).

2. How generated tasks were validated
- Filter 1: drop tasks whose criteria fall outside a predefined evaluation function library.
- Filter 2: o3 must solve the task both from the full description and from intent plus subtask instructions.
- LLM judge: five GPT-4.1 judges, majority vote (Table 2, p.8). Quote: "Completeness 81.33 93.71 / Appropriateness 88.33 88.08 / Both 72.67 83.77" (columns are + then Neo).
- Human curation: three annotators review and remove tasks. No removal counts or agreement figures are given.
- Human solve rate, Neo only (Table 3, p.9): "Human 92.31 90.00 91.67 91.43" for 1 / 2 / 3 apps / overall. Two annotators, "a randomly sampled subset"; the sample size is not stated.

3. How a task is graded
- Outcome only, on the final state. Quote (p.6): "After the agents complete each task, we save the entire file system and perform customized evaluations to verify correctness."
- Quote (p.7): "Our evaluation integrates exact matching, fuzzy matching, and execution-based methods... The output is considered to be successful if all the evaluation criteria are satisfied."
- Checks include keyword matching on documents and calendar events, Excel cell values, and code checks such as calendar conflicts. The metric is pass rate.
- The trajectory is not graded. Step counts are reported separately (Table 7, p.11): about 10-11 steps overall in every configuration.

4. Number of apps (Table 4, p.9; long-context setting, pass rate %)
- + split, 1-app to 3-app. Quote (p.10): "o3 drops from 72.83 to 30.36, GPT-4.1 from 55.91 to 12.50, and DeepSeek-R1 from 53.76 to 20.54."
- Neo split is milder: o3 68.33 to 59.06, GPT-4o 75.00 to 45.61.
- Best overall: o3 at 56.19 (+) and 61.26 (Neo). GPT-5 scores 54.00 and 55.96.

5. Context form (GPT-4o only, Tables 5-6, p.10)

| Setting | + split | Neo split |
|---|---|---|
| Full history | 33.67 (8,000 tokens) | 51.99 (6,700 tokens) |
| RAG, raw utterances, best | 29.41 (top-50, 730 tokens) | 38.74 (top-50, 915 tokens) |
| RAG, session summaries, top-5 | 24.00 (290 tokens) | 53.64 (2,200 tokens) |
| RAG, chunk summaries, top-25 | 33.33 (600 tokens) | 56.29 (1,360 tokens) |

- Summaries beat the full history only on Neo; on + the best summary result (33.33) is just under the baseline.
- More retrieval does not help past top-25. Quote (p.12): "Increasing top-k from 25 to 50 results in a slight performance decrease (from 56.29 to 54.97 on OdysseyBench-Neo)".

6. Repeats and intervals
- None. No repeated runs, seeds, temperature, confidence intervals or significance tests appear anywhere. Every figure reads as a single run.

LIMITS
- Many gaps are a handful of tasks (the Neo 1-app cell has n=60) with no intervals.
- The context-form study uses one model (GPT-4o) and one embedder (text-embedding-3-large).
- Circularity: GPT-4.1 generates and judges the data and is also evaluated; o3 is the solvability filter and also the top scorer. The paper says curators deliberately kept good tasks o3 could not solve, without counts.
- The paper describes "consistent performance degradation across all models", but its own Table 4 shows o3-mini on Neo rising from 39.44 (2-app) to 45.61 (3-app).
- No comparison against the original OfficeBench scores is shown, although the conclusion claims a gap versus atomic tasks.
- The agent harness, tool interface and step limits are not described.
- The failure taxonomy (four modes, p.12) is qualitative, with no frequencies.
- Table 2 does not say whether it describes the pool before or after filtering.
- No limitations section exists.

BUILDS ON: OfficeBench (Wang et al., 2024d) for tasks, environment and checkers; Magentic-One (Fourney et al., 2024) for the Neo pipeline. Contrasted with WebArena (Zhou et al., 2023), TheAgentCompany (Xu et al., 2024a) and τ-bench (Yao et al., 2024).

CODE: evaluation criterion format (p.18): `{"function": "evaluate excel cell value","args": {"file": "data/salary.xlsx","matches": [{"row": 5,"col": 2,"value": "200000"}]}}` (the underscore in the function name is probably lost in extraction).

FIGURES: Figure 1, p.2. It puts atomic tasks from five benchmarks beside one long-horizon task whose instructions are scattered over several days of dialogue with chitchat between them, which shows what multi-session evaluation means faster than prose.

PROBLEMS
- Table 6's chunk-summary rows for top-5 and top-10 are identical to Table 5's (30.11 / 29.47 / 12.50 / 23.33 and 40.86 / 34.74 / 16.96 / 30.00), and 30.11 is not reachable with 60 tasks. This looks like a copy-paste error; do not cite those rows.
- Table 5's utterance top-50 row (57.69 / 40.00 / 17.17, overall 29.41) is internally inconsistent: the per-app figures imply an overall near 37.
- "Overall" is labelled a macro-average, but the numbers match a task-weighted average.
- The text says "Soundness" where Table 2 says "Appropriateness".
- The human scores are consistent with 12/13, 9/10, 11/12 and 32/35, suggesting about 35 tasks. That is my inference, not printed.
- The appendix prompts contain imperative text (for example "DO NOT TERMINATE THE TASK..."). I treated it as paper content and ignored it.
- Rows are merged in the extraction of Tables 5-6 (for example "29.6710 1500"); I split the values by position.
